title: PLT jurisdiction keyword filter list
description: Curated linguistic filter used as stage 1 of the PLT ingestion filter chain. One file per jurisdiction. A document is selected when any term matches: there is no scoring, so every term carries the list alone and must be specific enough to justify that. See docs/core-document.md section 2.5.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file conforms to. 2.0.0 removed term weights and the score threshold: selection is a word search, and a term either selects a document or is not in the list.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction code. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for states; 'EU' for the European Union, which is treated as its own jurisdiction.

list_version.description: Semantic version of this list. Bump the minor version when terms are added or removed, the major version when matching semantics change.

updated.description: ISO 8601 date the list was last curated.

maintainer.description: Role or person responsible for curating this list. Curation is a content-manager responsibility.

languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes of the languages covered. Must cover every working language of the jurisdiction's courts.

notes.description: Free-text curation notes: known gaps, precision observations, decisions taken.

fields.description: The document fields a term is looked for in. A field absent from this list is not scanned at all, so the curator decides what counts as the text of a judgment.

exclusions.description: Patterns that veto a document outright however many terms matched. Use sparingly, for known homonym traps.

then.$comment: A regex term's 'term' is a pattern, and a pattern is not a name. Since every match is shown to the public as a label, a regex term has to say what to call it.

id.description: Stable identifier, prefixed with the language code. Never reuse an id for a different term; match provenance is stored against it, and it labels every case the term selected.

term.description: The term as it appears in court documents, in the source language. Also the public label a case carries when it matches, unless 'label' overrides it.

label.description: What to call this term where a reader sees it: on the case page, in the keyword filter, in a match report. Defaults to 'term'. Required when 'match' is 'regex', because a pattern such as '(?<!\\w)Ctgb(?!\\w)' is not a name and must never reach the public as one.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 code of the language this term is written in.

category.description: The kind of term this is. Stored on every match, so it is the second label a case carries and the one the public filters by.

match.description: 'word' matches on word boundaries; 'phrase' matches a whitespace-normalised multi-word sequence; 'substring' matches anywhere (use for compounding languages); 'regex' for the rare case the others cannot express.

case_sensitive.description: Set true only for short acronyms whose lowercase form is a common word. Inherited by every alias, so a case_sensitive term carries acronyms only: an ordinary word that inherits it matches solely the casing curated here.

case_sensitive_exception.description: Opts this term out of the acronym-only rule enforced on case_sensitive terms. Set it only where splitting the ordinary word into its own term would change which documents are selected rather than only structure. The loader rejects it on a term that is not case_sensitive, and on one that does not need it. See data/keywords/README.md, 'Known exceptions'.

aliases.description: Spelling variants, inflections and abbreviations of THIS term. An alias is reported under this term's id and label, so a different substance is never an alias: it is its own term.

requires.description: Term ids that must also match before this term counts. A term whose gate did not open selects nothing and labels nothing. This is what lets an active substance whose name is an ordinary word - water, beer, talc - stay in the list without admitting every judgment that says it.
